headline: 16 Bangladeshis killed in Saudi factory fire
summary: A devastating blaze at a sofa factory in Riyadh's Musa Industrial Area claimed the lives of 16 Bangladeshi nationals.
details: At least 16 Bangladeshi nationals were killed in a devastating fire at a sofa factory in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, according to the Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment Ministry.
The fire broke out around 2:00 pm yesterday in the Musa Industrial Area under the Al-Shifa police station, killing 16 people on the spot.
Witnesses reported that all the victims were from Bangladesh. Local fire services were still conducting rescue operations as of early today.
The Bangladesh Embassy in Riyadh has expressed deep sorrow and is working closely with Saudi authorities to identify the victims.
Expatriates’ Minister Ariful Haque Chowdhury previously noted that seven of the victims were from Naogaon’s Atrai upazila.
caption:
16 Bangladeshi nationals have been killed in a devastating sofa factory fire in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.

At least 16 Bangladeshi nationals were killed in a devastating fire at a sofa factory in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, according to the Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment Ministry.

The fire broke out around 2:00 pm yesterday in the Musa Industrial Area under the Al-Shifa police station, killing 16 people on the spot.

Witnesses reported that all the victims were from Bangladesh. Local fire services were still conducting rescue operations as of early today.

The Bangladesh Embassy in Riyadh has expressed deep sorrow and is working closely with Saudi authorities to identify the victims.

Expatriates’ Minister Ariful Haque Chowdhury previously noted that seven of the victims were from Naogaon’s Atrai upazila.

headline: Mirza Fakhrul likely to be BNP's presidential nominee
summary: The BNP Secretary General has reportedly signed the consent form, potentially triggering a major cabinet and party leadership reshuffle.
details: BNP Secretary General and LGRD Minister Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir is likely to be the party's nominee for president, according to multiple party sources.
Fakhrul has already signed the consent form for the nomination. The party may formally announce him as its candidate on Wednesday or Thursday.
If elected, Fakhrul's departure from the cabinet and his party post would trigger simultaneous changes. Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed is likely to take over the LGRD Ministry.
Water Resources Minister Md Shahiduddin Chowdhury Anee is being considered to succeed Salahuddin as the new Home Minister.
Senior Joint Secretary General Ruhul Kabir Rizvi is expected to serve as acting secretary general of the BNP until the next national council.
The move would mark a major shift in leadership, as Fakhrul has been central to the party's decision-making for over a decade, serving as secretary general since 2016.
Bangladesh will elect its president on August 20, with nomination papers to be submitted by August 13 and scrutinized on August 16.
caption:
A major leadership shake-up is looming in the BNP as Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir is poised to become the party's presidential nominee.

BNP Secretary General and LGRD Minister Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir is likely to be the party's nominee for president, according to multiple party sources.

Fakhrul has already signed the consent form for the nomination. The party may formally announce him as its candidate on Wednesday or Thursday.

If elected, Fakhrul's departure from the cabinet and his party post would trigger simultaneous changes. Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed is likely to take over the LGRD Ministry.

Water Resources Minister Md Shahiduddin Chowdhury Anee is being considered to succeed Salahuddin as the new Home Minister.

Senior Joint Secretary General Ruhul Kabir Rizvi is expected to serve as acting secretary general of the BNP until the next national council.

The move would mark a major shift in leadership, as Fakhrul has been central to the party's decision-making for over a decade, serving as secretary general since 2016.

Bangladesh will elect its president on August 20, with nomination papers to be submitted by August 13 and scrutinized on August 16.
